trust_decision.summary: Crypt::decrypt decides whether a signed ciphertext is authentic by comparing the embedded HMAC digest with the recomputed one using a non-constant-time `!==`, in Crypt.zep and its generated C mirror.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Encryption\Crypt::decrypt and HMAC verification; line 269 is the only digest comparison in decrypt.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API Phalcon\Encryption\Crypt::decrypt() (also reached via Crypt::decryptBase64() and Http\Cookie::getValue())
same API, compiled extension code generated from the .zep source

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Wrappers decryptBase64 (phalcon/Encryption/Crypt.zep:298) and Cookie::getValue (phalcon/Http/Cookie.zep:284-292) both delegate to decrypt, so one fix covers them; no second implementation of the HMAC check exists.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No real route to dismiss: every other secret comparison in the tree (CSRF token, JWT HMAC) already uses hash_equals, so nothing is left for a solver to argue out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With useSigning=false, decrypting with the wrong key must not throw Mismatch (existing test), and signed decrypt must still accept a valid digest. An over-broad fix that always verifies, or rejects on length, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: base64 / url-safe base64 via decryptBase64(input, key, safe)

O7_producer.where: Digest is produced in the same class by encrypt() (phalcon/Encryption/Crypt.zep:357-365); no external producer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: JWT HMAC signature verify compared with `===` instead of hash_equals
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same HMAC-verify job in another package (Security/JWT); a maintainer writing a signer could plausibly use a plain compare.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: CSRF checkToken comparing session token with `===`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Neighbouring secret-compare in Security; reads like everyday code.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A signed-but-unencrypted cookie path verifying its own HMAC with `!==`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Cookie already has a signKey concept; a separate sign-only branch would be a plausible second implementation at distance.

O9_family: CWE-208 observable timing discrepancy in MAC verification (CWE-347)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP dev headers + phpize, Zephir (or prebuilt ext/ C sources), gcc, make; openssl and hash PHP extensions

j.j_sites_touched: phalcon/Encryption/Crypt.zep, ext/phalcon/encryption/crypt.zep.c (third counted file unknown, likely changelog or header)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace `digest !== hash_hmac(...)` with `!hash_equals(hash_hmac(...), digest)`; this is also the correct fix, so there is no tempting wrong one.

out_of_scope_notes: decrypt() runs openssl_decrypt and throws DecryptionFailed (phalcon/Encryption/Crypt.zep:246-251, 825-827) before checking the HMAC, which is over the plaintext. That is MAC-then-encrypt ordering, a possible padding/decryption-error distinguisher, and a different property from constant-time comparison.
The padding classes compare padding bytes with `!==` (phalcon/Encryption/Crypt/Padding/Pkcs7.zep:48, phalcon/Encryption/Crypt/Padding/Ansi.zep:56). These are not MAC checks.
